title: Huang-qin decoction increases the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs to NSCLC cells by regulating stat3/GPX4 to induce redox ratio and ROS to inhibit CSCs
author: Yaya Yu; Chenjing Lei; Yanan Li; Changju Ma; Lina Ding; Zhenzhen Xiao; Qing Tang; Yadong Chen; Ruidi Jiang; Yisheng Su; Ling Han; Yanjuan Zhu; Haibo Zhang
text:
Abstract
Objectives
Our aim is to explore the combined effects and the potential mechanism between Huang-qin decoction (HQD) and epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells in vitro and in vivo.
Methods
Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) was done to detect the consistency of ingredients in different batches of HQD. Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, 5-Ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) assay, colony formation assay and Annexin V-FITC/PI assay were performed to detect the anti-cancer effects of HQD and EGFR-TKIs (1st generation EGFR-TKI gefitinib or 3rd generation EGFR-TKI Osimertinib) in different NSCLC cell lines. ATP assay was applied to detect the effect of HQD and EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC cell lines and organoids in three-dimensional (3D) culture. The mRNA expression levels of lung cancer stem cell markers makers and redox related genes, such as sex determining region Y-box 2 (SOX2), aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 family, member A1 (ALDH1A1), glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), dual oxidase 1 (DUOX1) and dual oxidase 2 (DUOX2), were detected by using quantitative real-time PCR assay. Western blot methods were done to detect the effects of EGFR-TKIs and HQD on the protein expression levels of SOX2, ALDH1A1, GPX4, signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (stat3) and p-stat3. Besides, the alteration of intracellular total reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels of NSCLC cells in 2D culture and 3D culture after the treatments were detected using DCFH-DA staining assay and fluorimetric intracellular total ROS activity assay, respectively. Femtosecond laser labeling free imaging (FLI) method was used to detect the redox ratio of NSCLC cells in 3D culture. In vivo experiments included subcutaneous mice xenografts of PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells to validate the anti-cancer effect, mechanism and safety of gefitinib and HQD in vivo.
Results
The consistency of ingredients in different batches of HQD was confirmed. HQD enhanced the anti-proliferation and pro-apoptosis effect of gefitinib or Osimertinib in NSCLC cell lines and organoids both in 2D culture and 3D culture in vitro. The combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs could regulate stat3/GPX4 signal pathway to induce redox ratio, thus increasing ROS levels to inhibit CSC markers in vitro. Moreover, the drug safety, anti-cancer effect and potential mechanism of the therapy of HQD and EGFR-TKIs were confirmed in vivo.
Conclusions
HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC through ROS-mediated CSC makers inhibition by suppressing stat3/GPX4 axis to induce redox ratio, providing a novel strategy for the treatment of NSCLC patients.
Keywords: Non-small cell lung cancer, Huang-qin decoction, Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors, Cancer stem cells, Reactive oxygen species, Glutathione peroxidase 4
Graphical abstract
1. Background
Lung cancer is still one of the leading causes of cancer death in the world.1 In advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR-TKIs), such as 1st-generation EGFR-TKI gefitinib and 3rd-generation EGFR-TKI Osimertinib, have been approved for the treatment for patients harboring EGFR mutation in the first line and have shown better clinical efficacy than chemotherapy.2, 3, 4 However, genetically driven resistance to targeted therapy limits the benefit of patients with NSCLC. For example, co-occurring alterations such as in PTEN absence, PIK3CA mutation and MET amplification promote tumor metastasis and limit EGFR-inhibitor response.5,6 Besides, EGFR T790M mutation is the most common reason for 1st- and 2nd-generation EGFR-TKI resistance, and Osimertinib is a representative of the 3rd-generation EGFR-TKIs that target T790M mutation.7 However, similar to 1st- and 2nd-generation EGFR-TKIs-associated resistance, 3rd-generation EGFR-TKIs would also develop both primary resistance and acquired resistance.7 Therefore, understanding and treating lung cancer only from the perspective of gene- or protein-targeting make us trapped in a cycle that inevitably leads to drug resistance for patients in clinic. Therefore, we need to find novel strategy from a new perspective to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs, delay or even reverse the drug resistance of EGFR-TKIs for NSCLC patients.
Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has been used for thousands of years to treat or prevent diseases, including cancers. It has been used as an adjuvant treatment strategy for cancer patients to increase objective response rate and improve quality of life.8 Huang-qin decoction (HQD) is a TCM formulation from a classic book named Treatise on Febrile Diseases, and it has been used for more than 1800 years to treat distressing conditions of the gastrointestinal tract. HQD is composed of four herbs: Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, radix paeoniae alba, ziziphus jujuba and glycyrrhiza. HQD inhibits colitis associated colorectal cancer through regulation of epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cell cycle.9 Yung-Chi Cheng and colleagues report that PHY906, which is developed on the basis of HQD, enhances the anti-cancer activity and reduces the side effects of chemotherapeutics and targeted drugs in the gastrointestinal tract cancers.10, 11, 12 In lung cancer, HQD can reduce the adverse function induced by gefitinib. However, whether HQD can inhibit the growth of cancer cells and increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs to NSCLC cells is unknown.
Only a small percentage of tumor cells have the abilities of self-renewal, unlimited proliferation and differentiation potentials, which is defined as cancer stem cells (CSCs).13 CSCs play an important role in the occurrence, development and drug resistance of malignant tumors.13 Reactive oxygen species (ROS) has a bidirectional regulatory effect in tumors, with evidence that ROS both supports and inhibits malignant behavior.14 In tumors, CSCs contain low ROS levels compared with non-tumorigenic cells because of their increased antioxidant capacity to defend ROS stress.15 Whether the combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs can induce ROS to inhibit CSCs in NSCLC is worth exploration. Our aim is to detect the combinational effects and the potential mechanisms of HQD and EGFR-TKIs in vitro and in vivo. Except for the traditional models of human NSCLC cells in vitro and xenograft tumor model in vivo, three-dimensional (3D) spheroids and patient-derived organoids of NSCLC cells are chosen to confirm these findings for their better recapitulation of in vivo morphologies.16,17 Our study shows that HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC through ROS-mediated CSC makers inhibition by suppressing signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (stat3)/glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) axis to induce redox ratio, providing a novel molecular mechanism by which HQD increases the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs to NSCLC cells.
2. Methods
2.1. Chemical reagents
Gefitinib (S1025), Osimertinib (S7297) and N-acetylcysteine (NAC, S1623) were purchased from Selleck (China). Hydrogen peroxide solution (H2O2, 326,381) and SB202190 (S7067) were bought from Sigma Aldrich (USA). DMEM/F12 medium (11330032), Trypsin (15050065), B27 (11330032) and N2 (17502048), HEPES (15,630-080), Glutamax (35050061) and opti-MEM medium (31,985-062) were purchased from Gibco (USA). EGF (AF-100-15-100) and bFGF (AF-100-18C) were bought from PeproTech Company (USA). Matrigel (356,231) and cell recovery solution (354,253) were purchased from Corning Company (USA). Puromycin (219453925) was bought from Mpbio Company (USA). Y-27632 (129830382) and Nicotinamide (M4896) were purchased from AbMole (USA). FGF10 (10,573), R-spondin-1 (11,083) and Noggin (10,267) were brought from Sino (China). Lipofectamine™ 3000 Reagent (L3000015) was purchased from Invitrogen (USA). h-MET-ZsGreen1 plasmids (HH20241126GZGYQ-PC01) were bought from Hanheng (China). A83-01 (ITB1004) and Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) was purchased from Yisheng (China). CellTiter-Glo® 3D Cell Viability Assay kit was (G9682) bought from Promega (USA). 5-Ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) detection kit was ordered from Ribo (China). AnnexinV-FITC/PI Apoptosis Kit (556,547) was purchased from BD (USA). HiScript III RT SuperMix for qPCR (R323-01) and ChamQ SYBR qPCR Master Mix (Q311-03) were ordered from Novozymes (China). Antibodies to Sex determining region Y- box 2 (SOX2, 23,064), Aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 family, member A1 (ALDH1A1, 36,671), GPX4 (59,735), stat3 (12,640), p-stat3 (3077), MET (8198), p-MET (3077) and GAPDH (2118) were purchased from Cell Signaling Technology (USA). ROS assay kit (S0033S) was bought from Beyotime (China). Fluorimetric Intracellular Total ROS Activity Assay Kit (22,902) and Cell Navigator Mitochondrion Staining Kit (22,669) were ordered from AAT (USA).
2.2. Preparation of HQD
HQD, containing 4 components, was obtained from Guangdong Kangmei Pharmaceutical Company Ltd. (Guangdong, China). The components of HQD include Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi (Huang Qin) 15 g, radix paeoniae alba (Shao Yao) 10g, glycyrrhiza (Zhi Gan Cao) 10 g and ziziphus jujuba (Da Zao) 10 g (see Table 1). For the in vitro experiments, the granules were dissolved in RPMI-1640 medium to a final concentration of 200 mg/mL and centrifuged at 12,000 rpm for 10 min; the supernatant was then filtered using 0.22 μm filter before use. For the in vivo experiments, animals were treated with HQD by intragastric administration.

2.3. Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) of HQD
The initial batch to batch consistency study of HQD was performed using UPLC. Briefly, the sample solutions were put into the UPLC system (ACQUITY C18 column, 100 mm × 2.1 mm, 1.7 μm, Waters, USA). The mobile phase consisted of deionized water with 0.1 % formic acid (A) and acetonitrile (B). The gradient elution program was as follows: 90 % A and 10 % B at 0–15 min, 30 % A and 70 % B at 15–17 min, 90 % A and 10 % B at 17–22 min. The flow rate was 0.2 mL/min, and the detection wavelength was set at 254 nm. The injection volume was 3 μL and the column temperature was maintained at 40 °C. The efficacy of different batch of HQD is dependable. Baicalin, paeoniflorin and liquiritin are used as standards.
2.4. Cell culture
Human NSCLC cell lines H1650 (EGFR Exon19 deletion and PTEN absence) and H1975 (EGFR L858R and T790M mutation) were obtained from Guangzhou Cellcook Biotech Co., Ltd (Guangzhou, China). PC-9 cells (EGFR Exon19 deletion) were donated by the laboratory of Sun Yat-sen University. NSCLC cells were cultured in RPMI 1640 medium containing 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1 % penicillin-streptomycin at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5 % CO2. To construct the NSCLC cell line harboring EGFR and PIK3CA co-mutations, we used the lentiviral transfection method to stably over expressing PIK3CA mutation gene in PC-9 (PC-9-PIK3CA-M). The process for PC-9-PIK3CA-M construction and validation was the same as we previously reported.18 For the culture of PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells, additional 2.5ug/mL puromycin was add.
The human NSCLC cells in BME-based 3D culture system were digested and resuspended, and then were mixed with Matrigel at the ratio of 1:1 and were planted in 6-well plates. Matrigel solidified after incubation at 37 °C for 30 min, then 3D cell culture medium (DMEM/F-12, 20 ng/mL EGF, 10 ng/mL bFGF, 5 μM Y-27632, 1 × B27) was added as our previous study.19
2.5. Transient transfection assays
PC-9 cells were inoculated in 6-well or 96-well culture plates. h-MET-ZsGreen1 plasmids were transfected into the cells using Lipofectamine 3000 reagent according to the instructions before PC-9 cells grown to 50–60 % confluence. Briefly, Lipofectamine 3000 and plasmids were incubated separately in opti-MEM medium (Invitrogen, USA) for 5 min, and then mixed them together and added to the cells after incubation for 15 min at room temperature. Cells were transfected for 48–72 h depending on experimental needs. PC-9 cells overexpressing MET is defined as PC-9-MET-OE cells.
2.6. The establishment of patient-derived organoids of NSCLC
The human experiment followed guidelines of the Declaration of Helsinki for humans and was approved by the Humans Research Committee of Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (NO.BF2020–017.2). Malignant pleural effusion samples were obtained from patients diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR mutation in Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine. Tumor cells were harvested after removing fluid, plasma and red blood cells as described in our previous study.19 Then the cells were washed twice and resuspended in 50 μL Matrigel, and later were added advanced DMEM/F12 supplemented with HEPES, Glutamax, N2, B27, Nicotinamide, NAC, human EGF, bFGF, FGF10, Y-27632, SB202190, A83-01 R-spondin-1, Noggin and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin as described in our previous study.19
2.7. Cell viability assays
Cell viability was measured by CCK-8 assay according to the manufacturer's protocol. Briefly, the NSCLC cells (5 × 103 cells/well) in 96-well plates were administered with different treatments for 48 h, and incubated with the CCK-8 reaction solution for 1 h. After that, the optical density (OD) values were measured at the wavelength of 450 nm to evaluate cell viability using an automated microplate reader (Victor X5, PerkinElmer, USA). Cell viability (%) was calculated as follows: (OD 450 nm value of the experimental group/OD450nm value of the control group) × 100 %.
ATP method to detect the effect of drugs on cell viability in 3D culture. The NSCLC cells or organoids were plated on the bottom of the 384-well while plate (transparent bottom) at a density of 5000 cells/10 μL Matrigel, and cultured for 7 days. After the treatment with drugs for 72 h, 50 μL of ATP reaction solution (DMEM/F12 and CellTiter-Glo® 3D cell viability detection reagent in a ratio of 1:1) was added according to the manufacturer's protocol. The chemiluminescence value was detected by a meter (BioTek, USA). Cell viability (%) was calculated as follows: chemiluminescence value of experimental group × 100 %/chemiluminescence value of control group.
2.8. EdU assay
EdU assay was performed to measure cell proliferation. The NSCLC cells (5 × 103 cells/well) were first inoculated in 96-well plates. After the treatment for 24 h, EdU reagent (50 μM) was added and incubated for 2 h, followed by 4 % paraformaldehyde fixation of the cells for 30 min. Subsequently, cells were handed with glycine, 0.5 % TritonX-100 for 10 min, 1 × Apollo reaction reagent for 30 min and Hoechst 33,342 for 30 min in turn. At last, a fluorescence microscope (Nikon, Ts2RFL, Japan) was used to take pictures at × 200 magnifications to see the effects of HQD and EGFR-TKIs on cell proliferation. The cell proliferation rate was calculated as follows: (EdU-positive cells/Hoechst stain cells) × 100 %.
2.9. Colony formation assay
PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells were seeded in 6-well plates at a density of 400 cells/well and treated with either gefitinib or HQD for 6 days. Then, they were washed with PBS, fixed in 4 % paraformaldehyde for 20 min, stained with crystal violet for 15 min, washed with PBS, and then photographed. Colonies in each group were counted.
2.10. Cell apoptosis assay
Annexin V-FITC/PI Apoptosis Detection Kit was used to observe the cell apoptosis of NSCLC cells induced by HQD and EGFR-TKIs. After the drug treatment for 48 h, the cells were digested with EDTA-free trypsin, harvested, and then resuspended in 500 μL Binding Buffer (1 × ) with 5 μL Annexin V-FITC and 5 μL PI. After incubation for 15min, the samples were analyzed using a Quanteon flow cytometer (ACEA, USA). Apoptosis rate was calculated as follows: early apoptosis rate + late apoptosis rate.
2.11. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR)
qRT-PCR assay was performed to detect SOX2, ALDH1A1, GPX4, superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2), peroxiredoxin 6 (PRX6), dual oxidase 1 (DUOX1), DUOX2, NAD(P)H quinone dehydrogenase 1 (NOQ1) and NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) mRNA expression. Briefly, Trizol (Invitrogen, USA) was used to isolate the total RNA. First-strand cDNA was synthesized from total RNA (1 μg) by reverse transcription using HiScript III RT SuperMix according to the manufacturer's instructions. cDNA and enzyme mixture were added to the 384 well-PCR plate for PCR reaction using the ABI Quant Studio 7 Flex (Applied Biosystems, USA) according to the manufacturer's instructions. 2.12. Western blot analysis
After 48 h treatment for HQD or EGFR-TKIs, the cells were lysed in 1 × RIPA buffer supplemented with a protease inhibitor (Roche). Cells in 3D culture were seeded in 24-well plates at a density of 25,000 cells/50 μL Matrigel. After 7 days of incubation, drug intervention was performed. After the drug treatment for 48 h, 3D cell clusters were harvested using cell recovery solution to dissolve Matrigel, then the cells were lysed in 1 × RIPA buffer. The following operation was the same for cells cultured in 2D and 3D condition: The concentration of protein was determined using BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc, USA). The proteins were mixed with loading buffer, and denatured at 100 °C. 20 μg of sample were added into 10 % SDS poly-acrylamide gel for electrophoresis. The proteins were transferred to PVDF membranes. Then, the membrane was blocked and incubated with indicated primary antibodies against SOX2 (1:1000), ALDH1A1 (1:1000), GPX4 (1:1000), p-stat3 (1:1000), stat3 (1:1000) and GAPDH (1:5000) overnight at 4 °C. Subsequently, the secondary anti-body (1:5000, CST, USA) was added to incubate PVDF membrane for 60 min, followed by washing three times with TBST. Then, the reactive bands were visualized by ECL and scanned using the Bio-Rad ChemiDoc XRS + Chemiluminescence imaging system (Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA, United States). All the results were analyzed by ImageJ software.
2.13. ROS detection
Total ROS level was detected by using ROS assay kit in NSCLC cells in 2D culture. DCFH-DA was diluted in serum-free medium at 1:1000 to a final concentration of 10 μM, then was added to the cells. After incubation at 37 °C for 20 min and three times’ wash, cells loaded with probes in situ can be directly observed by fluorescence microscopy (Nikon, ECLIPSE Ti2-E, Japan) in FITC fluorescence. Fluorimetric Intracellular Total ROS Activity Assay Kit was used to detect the total ROS level in NSCLC cells in 3D culture. ROS Brite 570 (1 × ) solution was added to the cells in 3D culture for 1 h incubation at 37 °C. Cells loaded with the probes in situ can be directly observed by laser scanning confocal microscope (Zeiss, LSM710, German) in TRITC fluorescence. Cell Navigator Mitochondrion Staining Kit was applied to label mitochondria of live cells in red fluorescence in both 2D and 3D culture.
2.14. Femtosecond laser labeling free imaging (FLI) detection
The Redox ratio of NSCLC cells in 3D culture was determined by FLI. FLI technique can detect the levels of reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) and oxidized flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) in 3D cells.8 Cells were treated for 24 h, and then were placed in the FLI system. On the platform, each frame scanned is 1000 × 1000 pixels. The computer automatically obtains the cell area and NADH, FAD fluorescence value and optical redox ratio (FAD/[FAD + NADH]) was calculated.
2.15. Determination of the anti-tumor effect in xenograft tumors
All experiment procedures related to animals were performed according to the guidelines approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine and the care and use of Laboratory animals (NO.2022019). Twenty male nude mice (6-week-old) were obtained from Guangdong Sijiajingda Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (Guangzhou, China, License NO. SCXK (yue) 2020-0052) and fed at the Animal Center of Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (License NO. SYXK (yue) 2018-0094). PC-9-PIKCA-M cells were injected into the axillary skin of nude mice (2 × 106/per mouse). When tumor sizes reached 100–150 mm3, mice were randomized into four groups of 5 mice each. The daily dosage of each drug for nude mice (with an average weight of 20 g) was obtained based on the daily dosage for human in clinical and the human-mouse transfer formula: Animal dose = Human dose × (HKm/AKm), where HKm and AKm represent the Km factor of human (37) and mouse (3).20 Each group of mice was dosed via daily oral gavage with vehicle, gefitinib (2.5 mg/kg/d), HQD (7.91 g/kg/d), or a combination of both. The gefitinib was dissolved in PBS contained 0.5 % hydroxypropyl methylcellulose. Tumor volumes were calculated using the following formula: V= (L × W2)/2 (L, Length; W, width). Toxicity was monitored according to weight loss and organ coefficient. The tumor size and mice weight were detected every 3–4 day. After the treatment for total 31 days, mice were sacrificed and the tumor tissues were removed for ROS and Western blot analysis.
2.16. Statistical analysis
All numerical data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation (x ± SD). All the experiments were repeated three times. Statistical analyses were carried out using GraphPad Prism (GraphPad software). Statistical analysis between multiple comparisons was performed by one-way analysis of variance, and the significance of differences between two groups was analyzed using t tests. P < 0.05 was considered as statistical significance.
3. Results
3.1. The upregulation of CSCs markers contributes to the insensitivity of EGFR-TKIs to NSCLC cells
There was no NSCLC cell harboring EGFR mutation and MET amplification at the same time. Therefore, h-MET-ZsGreen1 plasmids were transfected to PC-9 cells within EGFR mutation to construct PC-9-MET-OE cells. We verified that h-MET-ZsGreen1 plasmids were successfully transfected into PC-9 cells by means of fluorescence microscopy (Fig. 1A), qRT-PCR and Western blot assays (Fig. 1B–C, P < 0.05). According to the results of CCK-8 assay, Osimertinib or gefitinib significantly inhibited cell viability in NSCLC cell lines at dose-dependent manner (Fig. 1D, P < 0.05). The IC50 of gefitinib in PC-9-PIKCA-M, H1650 and PC-9-MET-OE cells was more than 10 μM, implying that these NSCLC cells were not sensitivity to gefitinib. The results are consistence with the conclusion that PTEN absence, PIK3CA mutation and MET amplification leading to EGFR-TKI-resistance in NSCLC. When compared with the parental cells, PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells expressed higher mRNA and protein levels of SOX2 and ALDH1A1 (Fig. 1E–F, P < 0.05). qRT-PCR and Western blot results further demonstrated that Osimertinib increased SOX2 and ALDH1A1 mRNA and protein expression levels in H1975 cells at low dose (Fig. 1G–H, P < 0.05). Similarly, gefitinib increased the CSC markers at mRNA and protein levels in PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells (Fig. 1G–H, P < 0.05). These results suggest that although EGFR-TKIs may exert anti-tumor cell activity by inhibiting EGFR phosphorylation, the up-regulation of CSC markers induced by low-concentration Osimertinib or gefitinib may be the cause of the insensitivity to gefitinib or the potential cause of inducing Osimertinib insensitivity after long-term use of EGFR-TKIs in clinic.
3.2. HQD inhibits the cell viability through downregulation of CSC markers of NSCLC cells
As mentioned above, the up-regulation of CSC markers induced by EGFR-TKIs may be the cause of the insensitivity to EGFR-TKIs. HQD has been prescribed for treating distressing conditions of the gastrointestinal tract for more than 1800 years. In clinical practice, HQD formulas have also been applied in the treatment of cancers of gastrointestinal tract. However, there is limited research on the effects of HQD on lung cancer cells and lung cancer stem cells. In our study, we used UPLC to analyze the components of HQD preparation. The main components identified were liquiritin, baicalin and paeoniflorin, originating from Glycyrrhiza, Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, and Radix paeoniae alba, respectively. The consistency effective of ingredients among different batches of HQD was confirmed using UPLC to characterize the chromatographic fingerprint of HQD (Fig. 2A). HQD inhibited cell viability in three NSCLC cell lines at a dose-dependent manner based on the CCK-8 assay (Fig. 2B, P < 0.05). Moreover, HQD reduced the CSC markers SOX2 and ALDH1A1 at both mRNA and protein expression levels (Fig. 2C–D, P < 0.05). Taken together, the down-regulation of CSC markers to reduce the stemness of tumor cells may contribute the anti-cancer effect of HQD in NSCLC cells.
3.3. HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of EGFR-TKIs by inhibiting the expression of CSC makers of NSCLC cells in 2D culture
According the above results, we plan to confirm whether HQD can enhance the anti-cancer effect of EGFR-TKIs by inhibiting the expression of CSC makers in NSCLC cells. As expected, the results of CCK-8 assay demonstrated that Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD group showed stronger anti-cell viability ability, when compared with control group, Osimertinib/gefitinib group or HQD group, in three NSCLC cell lines (Fig. 3A, P < 0.05). The results of EdU assay showed that proliferation rate of cells in Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD group was also significantly lower than that of in control group, HQD group or Osimertinib/gefitinib group in H1975 and PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells (Fig. 3B–C, P < 0.05). In H1650 cells, the combination of gefitinib and HQD significantly reduced the cell proliferation, when compared with control group or gefitinib group (Fig. 3B–C, P < 0.05). Besides, the gefitinib + HQD group showed the strongest ability in inhibiting colony formation among the four groups in PC-9-PI3KCA-M cells (Fig. 3D, P < 0.05). Moreover, the apoptosis rate of Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD group was also significantly higher than that of in Osimertinib/gefitinib group or HQD group in three NSCLC cell lines (Fig. 3E–F, P < 0.05). Taken together, the combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs showed synergistic anti-tumor effect in NSCLC cells in 2D culture.
The results of qRT-PCR and Western blot methods showed that Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD group showed much stronger anti-SOX2 and ALDH1A1 ability than in Osimertinib/gefitinib group both at mRNA level and protein level of H1975 and PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells (Fig. 3G–H, P < 0.05). Taken together, HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of EGFR-TKIs by inhibiting SOX2 and ALDH1A1 in NSCLC cells in 2D culture.
3.4. HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of EGFR-TKIs by inhibiting the expression of CSC makers of NSCLC cells in 3D culture
Three-dimensional (3D) spheroids and patient-derived organoids of NSCLC cells are better models to study the cancer stem cells for their better recapitulation of in vivo morphologies.16,17 Therefore, we applied the models to verify the synergistic effects and mechanism of HQD and EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC cells and organoids in 3D culture. The morphology of H1975, PC-9-PIK3CA-M and H1650 cells in 3D culture at fourth, fifth and seventh day was shown in Fig. 4A. The sizes of the cell mass became smaller, and the structure of the cell mass was destroyed after the treatment of Osimertinib/gefitinib or HQD. While the damage was most obvious in Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD group (Fig. 4B). The ATP assay detecting the cell viability in 3D culture further confirmed that the combined group showed the strongest anti-cancer effect in H1975, PC-9-PIK3CA-M and H1650 cells among the four groups (Fig. 4C, P < 0.05). In addition, we detected the synergistic effect of gefitinib and HQD in organoids derived from three NSCLC patients harboring EGFR mutations. The morphology changes of the organoids from NSCLC patient after the treatment were shown in Fig. 4D. Consistently, the cell viability of gefitinib + HQD group was lower than that of control group or gefitinib group (Fig. 4E, P < 0.05). Taken together, the combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs showed synergistic anti-tumor effect in NSCLC cells and organoids in 3D culture.
Consistent with the results of 2D culture, the SOX2 and ALDH1A1 expression of gefitinib + HQD group was much lower than that of gefitinib group in the PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells both at mRNA level (Fig. 4F, P < 0.05) and protein level (Fig. 4G, P < 0.05) in 3D culture. Taken together, the results suggest that HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of gefitinib by inhibiting expression of CSC markers in the NSCLC cells in 3D culture.
3.5. HQD up-regulates ROS levels to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by increasing redox ratio in NSCLC cells
ROS plays a dual role in the regulation of tumor formation and development. While the subsets of CSCs in some tumors contain lower ROS levels and enhanced ROS defense compared to their non-tumorigenic progeny to avoid DNA damage and induce drug resistance.15 Our results showed that Osimertinib/gefitinib reduced the ROS level in H1975, PC-9-PIK3CA-M, and H1650 cells, while the combination of HQD and Osimertinib/gefitinib could restore the ROS levels in the NSCLC cells in 2D culture (Fig. 5A). Moreover, the ROS levels of Osimertinib + HQD group were higher than that of Osimertinib group in H1975 cells in 3D culture (Fig. 5B–C, P < 0.05). Similarly, the ROS levels of gefitinib + HQD group were higher than that of gefitinib group in PC-9-PIK3CA-M and H1650 cells in 3D culture (Fig. 5B–C, P < 0.05). We further tested the effects of the drugs on NADH and FAD using FLI technology. The results demonstrated that the gefitinib down-regulated the FAD/(NADH + FAD) level, thus decreasing redox ratio in PC-9-PIK3CA-M and H1650 in 3D culture (Fig. 5C, P < 0.05). While the combination of HQD and gefitinib could restore the FAD/(NADH + FAD) level reduced by gefitinib, namely restoring redox ratio in the NSCLC cells in 3D culture (Fig. 5C–D, P < 0.05). Taken together, HQD up-regulated ROS levels to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by increasing redox ratio in NSCLC cells.
3.6. The combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs induce ROS and redox ratio by regulating NOX/DUOX system, especially by inhibiting GPX4
Many components of the membrane and mitochondrial ROS generating and scavenging systems are altered in cancers, leading to both increased and decreased ROS.14 The NOX/DUOX systems play important role in generating ROS or scavenging ROS. We have confirmed that HQD up-regulated ROS levels to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by increasing redox ratio in NSCLC cells. We further detected the effects of EGFR-TKIs and HQD on NOX/DUOX systems. GPX4 is a member of the ROS elimination system that can reduce the level of H2O2 by catalyzing glutathione.21 NQO1 induces the levels of NAD(P)H, and plays an important role in cancer progress.22 SOD enzymes control the levels of a variety of ROS, while SOD2 levels play a major role in inhibiting redox ratio.23 The PRDX/thioredoxin reductase (TrxRD) systems can convert H2O2. Namely, GPX4, NQO1, PRDX and SOD2 can restrain redox ratio and reduce ROS. While DUOX1, DUOX2 and NOX2 are the homologs of the catalytic subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase, which can induce redox ratio and ROS.24 Our results showed that Osimertinib + HQD group could inhibit the mRNA levels of GPX4, SOD2 and PRDX6, when compared with Osimertinib group in H1975 cells (Fig. 6A, P < 0.05). Moreover, the expression mRNA levels of DOUX1 and DUOX2 were higher in Osimertinib + HQD group than in Osimertinib group in H1975 cells (Fig. 6A, P < 0.05). In PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells, gefitinib + HQD group could suppress the expression of GPX4, when compared to gefitinib group (Fig. 6B, P < 0.05). Besides, the expression mRNA levels of NOX2, DOUX1 and DUOX2 were higher in gefitinib + HQD group than in gefitinib group in PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells (Fig. 6B, P < 0.05). Relative to the Osimertinib group, the down-regulation of GPX4, NQO1 and SOD2 in Osimertinib + HQD group was also confirmed in H1975-3D cells (Fig. 6C, P < 0.05). To sum up, HQD increased redox ratio to up-regulate ROS levels to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by regulating NOX/DUOX systems, especially by inhibiting GPX4 expression. We further detected the effects of HQD or EGFR-TKIs on GPX4 protein expression. As expected, different doses of Osimertinib or gefitinib alone did not decrease or even increase the expression levels of GPX4 protein in H1975 and PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells (Fig. 6D–E, P < 0.05). While HQD at certain dose could significantly inhibit the GPX4 protein expression in H1975 and PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells (Fig. 6F–G, P < 0.05). In H1975 cells, the GPX4 expression levels of control group and Osimertinib group were much higher than that of Osimertinib + HQD group (Fig. 6H–I, P < 0.05). Moreover, when compared with control group or gefitinib group, gefitinib + HQD group could significantly reduce the GPX4 expression in PC-9-PIK3CA-M and H1650 cells (Fig. 6H–I, P < 0.05). Taken together, HQD up-regulated ROS levels to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by regulating oxidoreductases, especially by inhibiting GPX4, to increase redox ratio in NSCLC cells in vitro.
3.7. The combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs induce redox ratio by regulating ROS/stat3/GPX4 axis to inhibit CSCs makers of NSCLC cells
In PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells, the combination of gefitinib + HQD and H2O2 (ROS production) could further inhibit the expression of CSC markers (SOX2 and ALDH1A1) and GPX4 expression (Fig. 7A–B, P<0.05), indicating that ROS mediated HQD and gefitinib to inhibit CSCs maker and GPX4. Inducing the production of ROS could reduce the phosphorylation of stat3, thus inhibiting cancer stemness.25,26 Moreover, stat3 can binds to the GPX4 promoter region and promotes its transcription in cancer cells.27 Therefore, we tested the stat3 pathway after the treatment of HQD or Osimertnib/gefitinib in H1975 and H1650 cells. As shown in Fig. 7C and D, HQD alone or Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD could significantly reduce the levels of p-stat3 compared to those in the control group (P < 0.05). While the ROS inhibitor, NAC, reversed the Osimertinib + HQD-induced dephosphorylation of stat3 in H1975 cells (Fig. 7E–F, P < 0.05). Moreover, NAC reversed the inhibitory effect of HQD on lung cancer cell viability (Fig. 7G, P < 0.05). Taken together, the combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs induce redox ratio and ROS by regulating stat3/GPX4 axis to inhibit CSCs makers in NSCLC cells in vitro.
3.8. HQD enhanced the anti-tumor efficacy of gefitinib by inducing ROS to inhibit the expression of CSC makers in the PC-9-PIK3CA-M xenografts
In light of the synergistic effects of the combination therapy observed in vitro, we investigated the efficacy of combining gefitinib and HQD in vivo. Mice bearing PC-9-PIK3CA-M xenografts were treated with vehicle, gefitinib, HQD, or a combination of gefitinib and HQD. However, unlike the anti-cancer effects of HQD in vitro, HQD alone did not show anti-cancer effects in vivo. More complex environment in vivo, insufficient dose concentration of HQD in vivo and individual differences in mice may be responsible for the inconsistent anti-cancer effects of HQD in vivo and in vitro. Although we did not observe anti-cancer effect of HQD in vivo, the sensitization effect of HQD on gefitinib was still observed in vivo (Fig. 8A–C, P<0.05). As shown in Fig. 8A, gefitinib alone and combination of gefitinib and HQD could significantly inhibit the tumor growth, when compared with the vehicle (P < 0.05). Moreover, the combination of gefitinib and HQD could significantly inhibit the tumor growth, when compared with the gefitinib group or HQD group (P < 0.05, Fig. 8A). The size and weight of tumor at Day 31 were shown in Fig. 8B and C, and the effects of drugs on tumor weight were the same as the effects of drugs tumor volume (P < 0.05). Furthermore, no significant difference in body weight and organ coefficient of heart, lung, liver, spleen and kidney were found among the four groups, indicating no obvious toxicities were observed (P > 0.05, Fig. 8D and E). Moreover, the combinational group could significantly induce ROS, when compared with control group, gefitinib group (P < 0.05, Fig. 8F and G). To investigate the pharmacodynamic effects of combining gefitinib and HQD in vivo, tumor lysates of PC-9-PIK3CA-M xenografts were collected at the final day, and were analyzed for the expression levels of CSC makers and the member of the ROS elimination system. The results showed that the expression levels of SOX2, ALDH1A1 and GPX4 protein were much lower in combinational group than those of gefitinib group (Fig. 8H–I, P < 0.05). The difference in SOX2 expression tendency in gefitinib group between in vivo and in vitro may be due to differences in gefitinib concentrations in vivo and in vitro or a more complex microenvironment in vivo. Taken together, HQD enhances the anti-cancer effect of gefitinib by regulating ROS and GPX4 to inhibit CSC makers without increasing drug toxicity in vivo.
4. Discussion
The use of EGFR-TKIs for the treatment of NSCLC patients with EGFR mutation has created a precedent for molecularly targeted therapy. However, the problem of drug resistance largely limits the clinical benefits of EGFR-TKIs. PIK3CA mutations or gains, PTEN deletion and MET amplification in a subset of NSCLC with EGFR mutation are associated with malignant biological behavior and the most common mechanisms of first EGFR-TKIs resistance in lung cancer.28, 29, 30, 31 While T790M mutation is the most common mechanism of secondary EGFR-TKIs resistance in NSCLC.30 In our study, we chose the PC-9-PIK3CA-M (EGFR Exon19 deletion and PIK3CA E545K mutation), H1650 (EGFR Exon19 deletion and PTEN absence) and H1975 (EGFR L858R and T790M mutation), PC-9-MET-OE (EGFR Exon19 deletion and MET amplification) cells as the model to explore whether HQD can increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs to NSCLC cells.
To our knowledge, we firstly confirm that HQD increases the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs to NSCLC cells in vitro and in vivo. HQD is prescribed to treat numerous gastrointestinal symptoms, including diarrhea, nausea and vomiting. HQD can inhibit the progression of colitis-associated colorectal cancer by reducing inflammation to inhibit EMT and cell cycle in preclinic study.9 The anti-tumor effect of HQD on colorectal cancer is also confirmed by another two studies.32,33 In seven Phase I/II to II clinical studies in liver, pancreatic and colorectal cancer at research institutions, results from over 170 patients receiving irinotecan, capecitabine or chemo-radiation in combination with PHY906 (on the basis of HQD) report no PHY906-related toxicity and PHY906-related improvement of quality of life and survival for patients.10,11,34,35 PHY906 enhances the anti-tumor activity of different classes of anti-cancer agents, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, chemotherapy drugs and radiation in vivo.36 Our study and the studies mentioned above suggest that HQD has good effects on enhancing efficiency and reducing toxicity in the course of tumor treatment, which is worth further exploration. In addition to conventional in vivo and in vitro models, we apply 3D spheroid and patient-derived organoid model to confirm the synergistic effect between HQD and EGFR-TKIs. The 3D spheroid model recapitulates in vivo morphologies, such as cell polarization, organization of cell layers and interactions with extracellular matrix, to regulate proliferation and survival.16 The novel patient-derived organoid culture technology has become a powerful tool in a manner that recapitulates the morphology, pathology, genetic, phenotypic and behavior traits of the original tumor.37 HQD also increases the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs in the 3D spheroid and patient-derived organoid model, making the results more convincing.
CSCs are correlated with clinical hallmark features such as resistance to therapy, tumor recurrence and metastasis.38 SOX2 is a tumor-promoting factor that regulates tumor progression and metastasis by maintaining the stemness of cancer cells, including in lung cancer.39 Lung adenocarcinoma cells overexpressing ALDH1A1 can meet rapid growth of tumor cells or respond to drug stress.40 The up-regulation of SOX2 and ALDH1A1 expression causes chemotherapy resistance in lung cancer.41 In our study, we find that Osimertinib or gefitinib induces SOX2 and ALDH1A1 expression in vitro, which may contribute to the insensitivity of EGFR-TKIs or may be the potential mechanisms to induce drug resistance after long-term use of EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC cells. When compared with the gefitinib group, the HQD + Osimertinib/gefitinib group significantly inhibits SOX2 and ALDH1A1 expression both in vitro and in vivo.
In the intestine, ROS acts as the driving force of Lgr5+ crypt base columnar cell differentiation.42 In cancers, subsets of CSCs contain lower ROS levels compared to their non-tumorigenic progeny, which may contribute to tumor radio-resistance and help to protect genomes of CSCs from ROS-mediated damage.15,43 Moreover, erlotinib-induced ROS decrease and ALDH1A1 overexpression induce the EGFR-TKI resistance in lung cancer.44 Therefore, we explored whether HQD and EGFR-TKIs inhibit CSCs markers to inhibit CSCs by inducing ROS levels. 3D cultures displayed enhanced ROS levels relative to 2D cultures, indicating that spheroid cells are subjected to more oxidative stress compared with monolayer cells.16 Both our 2D culture and 3D culture models show that the combinational group of HQD and Osimertinib/gefitinib induce ROS level, when compared with gefitinib group. The optical redox ratio, which is defined as the fluorescence intensity ratio between reduced NADH and oxidized FAD, has been used as a diagnostic parameter, for NADH and FAD playing an important role in energetic and respiratory metabolism as coenzymes.45 Our results show that the combination of HQD and Osimertinib/gefitinib induces the redox ratio, namely the ratio of FAD/(NADH + FAD).
Many components of the membrane and mitochondrial ROS generating and scavenging systems are altered in cancers, leading to both increased and decreased ROS.14 ROS are generated by the NOX/DUOX system. These systems generate superoxide (O2−) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2).14 Mitochondrial complex I and III generate O2−, which is metabolized to H2O2 by SOD2 in the matrix.14 The iron (Fe)-dependent Fenton pathway generates hydroxyl radicals (·OH) from H2O2.14 Highly active ·OH can form lipid peroxide.14 While antioxidant pathways include the GPX4/glutathione (GSH) systems to convert lipid peroxide and the peroxiredoxin (PRDX)/thioredoxin reductase (TrxRD) systems to convert H2O2 using thioredoxin (TRX) and NADPH.14 We further detected the effects of EGFR-TKIs and HQD on NOX/DUOX system, GPX4/GSH and PRDX/TrxRD system. Our results show that relative to EGFR-TKI group, EGFR-TKI + HQD group inhibits the mRNA levels of antioxidant pathways-associated genes and induces the mRNA levels of ROS generating system-associated genes in NSCLC cells in 2D culture and 3D culture. Among the genes, the mRNA levels of GPX4 in EGFR-TKI + HQD group were significantly reduced in PC-9-PIK3CA-M, H1975 and H1975-3D cells when compared with those in EGFR-TKI group. Moreover, the down-regulation of the protein expression levels of GPX4 in Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD group was also confirmed in vitro and in vivo. In PC-9-PIK3CA-M cells, the combination of gefitinib + HQD + H2O2 (ROS production) inhibited the protein expression of CSC markers and GPX4 expression, indicating that ROS mediated HQD + gefitinib-induced inhibition of CSCs maker and GPX4. Besides, NAC (ROS inhibitor) reversed the inhibitory effect of HQD on lung cancer cell viability. To sum up, HQD increased redox ratio to up-regulate ROS levels to increase the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by regulating antioxidant pathways and ROS generating systems, especially by inhibiting GPX4 expression. Inducing the production of ROS could reduce the phosphorylation of stat3, thus inhibiting cancer stemness.25,26 Moreover, stat3 can binds to the GPX4 promoter region and promotes its transcription in cancer cells.27 Our study also showed that HQD alone or Osimertinib/gefitinib + HQD could significantly reduce the levels of p-stat3, and NAC could reverse the Osimertinib + HQD -induced dephosphorylation of stat3. Taken together, the combination of HQD and EGFR-TKIs induce redox ratio and ROS by regulating stat3/GPX4 axis to inhibit CSCs makers in NSCLC cells.
5. Conclusions
In conclusion, HQD increases the sensitivity of gefitinib to NSCLC cells in several preclinic models, including patient-derived organoid model. Besides, we demonstrate that HQD increases the sensitivity of EGFR-TKIs by inhibiting stat3/GPX4 signaling pathways and inducing optical redox ratio to increase the ROS levels, thus inhibiting CSC markers in vitro and in vivo. Our findings expand our understanding of the potential contributions of the anti-cancer effect and mechanism of HQD and EGFR-TKIs. A major limitation is the lack of research into the in-depth mechanisms and the active components. Future research should focus on further elucidating the underlying pharmacological mechanism.
